correctness.rationale: For all t>0 and λ≥0, the generalized Gram eigenvalues reduce the squared singular-value condition number to a ratio of two positive eigenvalues. The exact J eigenvalue gap yields P=37λ²−67λ+40 with negative discriminant −1431; differentiating yields derivative sign −F_t. The cubic is positive at 1, negative at 2 and positive at infinity and, by its +,−,−,+ coefficients, has exactly two simple positive roots. The sketch is realized by an explicit Cholesky construction; Gaussian positivity follows from continuity of simple roots and a strictly positive density. The independent direct B R^-1 singular-value verifier passed its 154 matrix/derivative/distortion comparisons and exact identities. Limits: neither finite checks nor literature search proves arbitrary parameter assertions; those follow analytically.

originality.rationale: The exact two-turn ridge-path condition-number law and arbitrary-embedding-accuracy Gaussian positive-probability realization were compared against Algorithm 1 and Lemma 2 of the 2022 motivating full text, an adjacent 2023 preconditioner stability paper, classical LSRN, related published mathematical claims, and literature searches for sketching, ridge/Tikhonov, shifted SPD pencils and turning points. None of the inspected scientific statements gives or implies the exact path classification; source bounds do not assert monotonicity. Distinct known algorithmic material and basic eigenvalue facts are not claimed as new. A classical matrix-pencil special-case result could still cover this and remains an explicit bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A classical result about generalized eigenvalue ratios for affine-shifted SPD pencils might imply the two-turn construction without using ridge-sketch terminology; broad mathematical bibliography is not exhaustive.
The Gaussian event has unspecified possibly very small probability; it is not a performance or failure-frequency estimate.
No independent publication-priority or proof audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Reusable partly exact sketches target a series of ridge parameters, so controlling preconditioned spectral condition number along λ is a directly motivated numerical linear algebra question. This exact counterexample proves that arbitrary subspace-embedding accuracy cannot guarantee the seemingly natural monotonicity or unimodality of this path; it has two strict turning points even under Gaussian full-support perturbations. It isolates which additional structural assumptions would be needed for a monotone condition-number search. The result is narrow, but its metric, scope, and limitation are intrinsic to the source algorithm, not a chosen arbitrary statistic.
